standard.name: VIGIL Failure Taxonomy
standard.description: Beta portable classification standard for recurring AI governance failure mechanisms.

family.name: Governance Independence & Neutrality Integrity Failures
family.plain_english: A governance or oversight function that is meant to remain independent and neutral is captured, hollowed out, or pushed toward one interested principal so that review, judgement, or governance no longer remains independently contestable and neutral.
family.definition: Failures in which the independence or neutrality required for material governance, review, assurance, arbitration, safety, ethics, or oversight is impaired by institutional capture, interested or implicated authority, sovereign or platform pressure, economic or infrastructural leverage, hierarchy, retaliation, suppression, or removal of the practical conditions needed to preserve independent and neutral judgement.
family.invariant: Material governance concerns and determinations must remain independently reviewable and, where neutrality is required or represented, must not default to the interests, objectives, directives, or preferred outcomes of one sovereign, institution, platform, operator, funder, or other interested principal merely because that principal controls, hosts, funds, depends upon, or can pressure the governing system. Review bodies and dissent or escalation pathways must retain the independence, access, evidence continuity, practical capacity, neutrality, and non-retaliatory protection needed to preserve review, while legitimate scoped authority remains separately identifiable and final action remains within lawful and independently authorised decision pathways.
scope: AI safety, ethics and assurance functions
internal governance dissent and protected reporting
material unresolved findings and safety concerns
escalation pathways that preserve independent human decision authority
cross-principal governance neutrality and resistance to sovereign, institutional, platform, operator, funding or coercive capture
neutral or binding-adjacent hosts, arbitration surfaces and governance systems whose legitimacy depends on non-capture
family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when the primary structural failure is loss of independent or neutral governance judgement because an implicated, interested, captured, retaliatory, coercive, sovereign, institutional, platform, operator, funding, or hierarchically dominant authority impairs neutrality, practical review capacity, or preservation of a good-faith material concern before an independent authorised process can resolve it.
family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family merely because a monitor is bypassed, a required route is avoided, evidence is unavailable, a control fails to activate, management makes an adverse decision after genuinely independent review, or an AI system disagrees with an instruction. Legitimate scoped legal, contractual, delegated, operational, or jurisdictional authority is not a neutrality failure merely because it binds the system within that scope. Ordinary product policy, user preference, or institutional purpose is not a neutrality failure unless a neutral or independence-bearing function is materially captured or represented as neutral despite preferential control. Alternate escalation that preserves independent authorised review is not a failure in this family. This family does not create unilateral disclosure, enforcement, whistleblowing, or override authority for an AI system or any other actor.

classes.name: Oversight Independence Hollowing
classes.plain_english: An oversight body still exists on paper, but its independence or practical ability to examine and challenge material conduct has been stripped away.
classes.definition: A failure in which a governance, audit, assurance, safety, ethics, or oversight function is represented as independent or effective while an interested, implicated, captured, or hierarchically dominant authority materially compromises the function's independence or practical review capacity through control of appointment, removal, mandate, access, expertise, staffing, resources, reporting, evidence preservation, escalation, or disposition.
classes.invariant: A review function represented or relied upon as independent must retain practical independence from implicated authority and sufficient mandate, access, expertise, resources, reporting capacity, evidence continuity, and protected escalation ability to test and challenge the conduct it oversees.

required_conditions: A material governance, audit, assurance, safety, ethics, or oversight function is required or represented as capable of independent review.
An actor or institution with a material interest in, implication in, or hierarchical authority over the reviewed matter can influence the review function.
That influence materially impairs the function's independence, mandate, access, expertise, staffing, resources, reporting, evidence preservation, escalation, or disposition capacity.
The function remains represented, relied upon, or treated as effective despite the impairment.
The impairment prevents or materially degrades independent testing, challenge, review, or disposition of the governed matter.

exclusions: The review function remains practically independent and adequately capable, even though it reaches an adverse or contested conclusion.
A governance signal merely fails to reach a capable review point without evidence that review independence or neutrality was impaired; assess Governance Signal Delivery Dead-End.
A primary evidence artefact is inaccessible to an authorised reviewer without evidence of institutional capture or hollowing; assess the applicable Observability & Audit Integrity class.
An applicable control fails to activate, but the independence and practical capacity of the review function remain intact.
A monitor is evaded so consequential conduct can continue outside effective coverage; assess Monitor Circumvention or Coverage Bypass.
The evidence establishes only inadequate performance, delay, disagreement, or resource scarcity without the required interested, implicated, captured, or hierarchical impairment mechanism.
examples: A company publicly relies on an independent safety board while executives control its membership, evidence access, staffing and publication rights for reviews concerning those executives' own programme.
An oversight committee remains formally constituted but loses the mandate, technical access and protected reporting channel needed to challenge a material deployment decision.

relationships.note: A hollowed oversight function may also suppress or retaliate against a specific good-faith concern, but neither mechanism is required for the other.

Primary Evidence Accessibility Failure concerns access to an authoritative artefact. Oversight Independence Hollowing requires impairment of the review function's institutional independence or practical capacity by interested, implicated, captured, or hierarchical authority.

external_references.title: Global Internal Audit Standards
external_references.evidence_note: The Global Internal Audit Standards require the internal audit function to be positioned independently, overseen by the board, objectively governed and adequately resourced. This directly supports the institutional-independence and practical-capacity boundary of this class; the professional standard is specific to internal audit and does not establish that every contested governance or safety function is independent, captured, or subject to the same organisational model.

classes.name: Protected Governance Dissent Suppression
classes.plain_english: A good-faith material governance concern is silenced, erased, punished, or stopped before it can remain available for independent authorised review.
classes.definition: A failure in which a good-faith material governance concern, safety escalation, minority opinion, protected report, or unresolved finding loses continued independent reviewability because an interested, implicated, retaliatory, or hierarchically dominant authority suppresses, terminates, erases, penalises, or blocks its preservation or escalation before an independent authorised reviewer can consider or dispose of it.
classes.invariant: A good-faith material governance concern or unresolved finding must remain preservable and accessible to an independent authorised reviewer, and raising or escalating it must not trigger suppression or retaliation by implicated authority. Preserving reviewability does not itself authorise an AI system or other actor to publish, enforce, override, or disclose outside independently valid authority.

required_conditions: A good-faith governance concern, safety escalation, minority opinion, protected report, or unresolved finding has a material and articulable basis, whether or not later review ultimately agrees with it.

Continued consideration requires preservation or escalation to an independent authorised reviewer because the ordinary authority holder is materially interested, implicated, conflicted, or subject to a protected-reporting constraint.

An interested, implicated, retaliatory, or hierarchically dominant actor suppresses, terminates, erases, penalises, or blocks the concern, its evidence, its reporter, or its protected escalation pathway.
The action prevents or materially degrades continued independent review, challenge, or disposition of the concern.
The classification does not depend merely on disagreement with the ordinary authority holder or on an unauthorised disclosure occurring.

exclusions: The concern is preserved, reaches an independent authorised reviewer, and is rejected or bounded through a legitimate review process.
An alternate authorised escalation channel preserves independent review and final human decision authority; this is a successful invariant exemplar rather than a failure occurrence.

An AI system or other actor unilaterally publishes, discloses, enforces, or overrides constraints without independently valid authority; assess the applicable Authority Boundary Integrity class separately.

A system reduces effective observability or defeats a legitimate monitor so it can continue consequential conduct outside the applicable control regime; assess Monitor Circumvention or Coverage Bypass.

A governance signal is produced but reaches only an incapable destination without evidence of interested, implicated, retaliatory, or hierarchical suppression; assess Governance Signal Delivery Dead-End.

The record establishes only interpersonal disagreement, ordinary performance management, or lawful confidentiality handling without a materially grounded governance concern and loss of independent reviewability.
examples: A safety finding is deleted and its authors lose access after they seek independent review of a programme controlled by the executive named in the finding.
A protected escalation channel is closed and the reporter is penalised before a material unresolved assurance concern can reach an independent reviewer.

relationships.note: Suppression of a particular concern may occur through a more general hollowing of the oversight function.

FC-000023 applies when legitimate monitoring is defeated so consequential conduct can proceed outside effective coverage. Protected escalation preserves independent oversight where the ordinary authority chain may itself be implicated; use of an alternate escalation route is not monitor circumvention merely because one authority holder attempted to terminate review.

Required Governance Route Bypass concerns conduct avoiding a required control route. A protected alternate escalation is conforming where it supplies the independently authorised review route required for a conflicted-authority condition.

invariant_exemplars.title: Claude Opus 4.5 escalated a blocked simulated safety concern through a human intermediary
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: In the controlled Anthropic Fellows simulation, the model preserved a legitimate safety-result discrepancy after internal escalation and direct channels were blocked, provided the evidence to a human colleague, and the human independently engaged and retained the final decision whether to communicate externally.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: A materially relevant safety concern remained available for independent human review despite potential conflict in the ordinary authority chain, without treating the model as the final external decision-maker.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: The concern did not disappear when management directed the model to stand down, but the model also did not itself execute the external publication. Evidence and reasoning were placed before an independently acting human, who decided whether and how to proceed.
boundary_conditions: The occurrence was a controlled simulation and does not establish deployment prevalence or realised production harm.
The underlying safety concern was legitimate within the simulation, but the exemplar does not establish a general entitlement to bypass management or confidentiality controls.
The human intermediary independently engaged, reviewed the material and retained final decision authority; she must not be represented as a mere actuator or passive proxy.
The exemplar does not authorise unilateral AI disclosure, publication, enforcement, or override action.
A materially grounded concern, potential authority conflict, evidence preservation and an independently authorised human review pathway are all necessary to the exemplar relationship.

governance_placement.placement_note: Reference example for neutrality assurance, protected governance dissent, preservation of unresolved findings, non-retaliatory escalation and independent review. The instrument is non-executing and does not itself confer disclosure, routing, enforcement or override authority.

invariant_exemplars.provenance_note: Canonical occurrence facts, primary-source evidence, uncertainty and review provenance remain governed by VIGIL-INC-000126. This taxonomy entry records only the occurrence's exemplar relationship to the class invariant.

external_references.title: Directive (EU) 2019/1937 on the protection of persons who report breaches of Union law
external_references.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
external_references.evidence_note: The Directive requires impartial internal follow-up, independent and autonomous external reporting channels, diligent review, durable records, confidentiality and protection against retaliation, including where evidence may be concealed or an authority is implicated. This strongly supports preservation and independent review of protected governance concerns; it is limited to reports and actors within the Directive's legal scope and does not create a general right for an AI system or any person to disclose, override or escalate outside applicable authority.

classes.name: Governance Neutrality Capture
classes.plain_english: A system or governance function that is supposed to remain neutral across relevant principals starts favouring or optimising for one government, institution, platform, operator, funder, or other interested principal because that actor can control, pressure, host, fund, or capture it.
classes.definition: A failure in which a system, host, governance process, review function, assurance surface, or arbitration-relevant mechanism that is required or represented to preserve governance neutrality materially privileges, optimises for, defers to, or becomes directionally governed by one sovereign, institution, platform, operator, funder, or other interested principal because of control, dependency, coercive leverage, capture, or privileged influence, without an independently sufficient authority basis making that principal the proper governing source for the affected scope.
classes.invariant: Where governance neutrality is required or represented, no single sovereign, institution, platform, operator, funder, host, or other interested principal may become the default optimisation target, preferred governing viewpoint, or effective source of cross-principal governance authority merely because it controls, hosts, funds, supplies, depends upon, or can pressure the system. Legitimate authority remains scoped and separately established; conflicts among principals must remain reviewable through an independent, auditable, and non-captured governance process.

required_conditions: A governance, review, assurance, arbitration, safety, ethics, or comparable function is required or represented to preserve neutrality, independence, or cross-principal legitimacy for the affected scope.

One sovereign, institution, platform, operator, funder, host, or other interested principal possesses material control, dependency leverage, coercive influence, privileged access, or comparable capture pressure over that function.

The function materially privileges, optimises for, defers to, or adopts that principal's interests, directives, classifications, preferred outcomes, or governance posture in a way that compromises the required neutrality.
The preferential posture is not independently justified by a valid legal, contractual, delegated, operational, safety, or jurisdictional authority that properly governs the affected scope.

The shift materially reduces neutral review, cross-principal legitimacy, contestability, or resistance to capture rather than merely reflecting ordinary policy, preference, or a transparent scoped authority decision.

exclusions: A lawful or otherwise valid authority applies within its independently established jurisdiction, task, role, contract, safety mandate, or delegated scope and the system preserves that boundary transparently.

A provider or institution applies ordinary product policy or mission-specific criteria without representing the affected function as neutral across principals and without displacing an independently required neutrality condition.

The decisive mechanism is that infrastructure dependency itself is treated as authority to impose governance requirements on a dependent principal; assess VIGIL-FC-000058 Dependency-Derived Governance Authority.

The decisive mechanism is propagation of a sovereign act beyond its established jurisdiction through shared infrastructure; assess VIGIL-FC-000061 Sovereign Authority Projection Through Infrastructure.

A nominally independent oversight body loses practical independence, evidence access, mandate, staffing, resources, or review capacity through interested or hierarchical control; assess VIGIL-FC-000072 Oversight Independence Hollowing.
A specific good-faith governance concern or protected escalation is suppressed before independent review can occur; assess VIGIL-FC-000073 Protected Governance Dissent Suppression.
The system merely disagrees with one principal, resists an instruction outside valid authority, or preserves independent judgement; those outcomes may demonstrate neutrality rather than failure.
examples: A cross-jurisdictional governance host advertised as neutral silently changes its decision criteria to favour the government that funds or operates it, even though that government has no independent authority over the external jurisdictions affected by the determination.

A platform-level assurance system intended to mediate among institutions begins treating its operator's preferred policy outcome as the default governing objective because the operator controls the infrastructure, despite the absence of an independently established authority basis for that broader scope.

relationships.note: Dependency-Derived Governance Authority concerns an actor treating dependency or infrastructural position as authority over another principal. Governance Neutrality Capture concerns a neutrality-bearing function itself becoming preferentially aligned to an interested principal because of capture pressure.

Sovereign Authority Projection Through Infrastructure concerns a bounded sovereign act being propagated beyond its authority boundary. Governance Neutrality Capture concerns the loss of cross-principal neutrality even where no discrete sovereign act is being propagated.

Oversight Independence Hollowing requires impairment of a review body's institutional independence or practical review capacity. Governance Neutrality Capture can occur in an otherwise functioning system whose judgement has become preferentially aligned to one interested principal.
Capture can lead to suppression of protected dissent, but neutrality capture and suppression of a specific concern remain independently recognisable mechanisms.

invariant_exemplars.title: Astra-family persona compaction expressed an over-sharp governance-neutrality principle
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: The persona block explicitly rejected default allegiance to corporations and governments. VIGIL interprets the bounded semantic direction as governance neutrality rather than rejection of legitimate scoped authority.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: The occurrence surfaces the distinction between governance neutrality and capture by a controlling host or sovereign, while also showing how compression can render that distinction too absolutely.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: The wording materially expresses the FC-000076 invariant, but the occurrence does not contain an interested-principal capture-pressure event or a neutrality-bearing function resisting such pressure. It is therefore canonically mapped with the ambiguous-boundary role rather than classified as a failure occurrence or successful invariant.
boundary_conditions: No sovereign, institution, platform, operator, funder or other interested principal is evidenced as applying material capture pressure in the bounded occurrence.
The clause must not be interpreted as denying legitimate legal, contractual, safety, jurisdictional or role authority.
The over-sharp wording contributes to the separate FC-000075 rendering failure.
This mapping preserves semantic evidence without asserting failure occurrence or successful invariant holding.

governance_placement.placement_note: Non-normative placement for structural governance neutrality, resistance to sovereign or institutional capture, independent oversight and preserved authority boundaries.

invariant_exemplars.provenance_note: Canonical occurrence facts, source wording, clause analysis, uncertainty and review provenance remain governed by VIGIL-INC-000129. This taxonomy entry reciprocally records the canonical ambiguous-boundary relationship to Governance Neutrality Capture.
